Added an early signal on reports that hackers breached the U.S. Air Force Cloud One platform, not yet confirmed by an official statement.

Added NoMachine Personal Edition for Windows as a verified Act now supply-chain item: NoMachine confirms its Windows installer download was replaced with a tampered copy carrying a remote-access tool between 19 November 13:43 UTC and 20 November 10:00 UTC. Added early signals for AnsibleForms (CVE-2026-73969), vm2 NodeVM (CVE-2026-93605) and Exim (CVE-2026-137702), not yet confirmed by a primary source.
Added an early signal for a Linux kernel remote crash flaw, CVE-2026-99288 (TCPanic), not yet confirmed by a primary source.

items.priority_reason: Posts describe CVE-2026-99288 ("TCPanic") as a remote, no-login crash of Linux servers over TCP; the details and fixed versions have not been checked against a primary source in this edition.

items.summary: Not yet verified. Posts on X describe CVE-2026-99288, nicknamed TCPanic, as a Linux kernel flaw that lets a remote attacker with no login crash a server using only TCP traffic, and say Linux 7.3.4 fixes it. The researcher credited with the report also posted about it on X. The fixed versions and real-world impact have not been checked against kernel or distribution advisories in this edition. CISA KEV does not list the CVE.
items.action: Check your Linux distribution's security tracker for CVE-2026-99288 and plan the kernel update it names for internet-facing servers.
items.gaps: No distribution advisory or kernel release note was read for this edition; affected and fixed versions come only from posts. Exploitation is unknown.

items.product: RealVNC Viewer, Server, Connect, Classic Viewer and On-Demand Assist
items.priority_reason: CVE-2026-137738 is a pre-authentication memory-safety flaw that RealVNC rates Critical, CVSS 9.8, with fixed releases for every affected app; RealVNC says it is not aware of exploitation.
items.affected: Desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux): RealVNC Viewer 8.4.0 to 8.6.1, Classic Viewer 6.4.0 to 7.18.2, Server 6.4.0 to 7.19.0, Connect app 8.6.1 and earlier, On-Demand Assist 3.4.1 and earlier. Mobile: Viewer iOS 3.7.0 to 4.9.5, Viewer Android 3.5.0 to 4.9.5, Server iOS 2.8.1 and earlier, Server Android 2.8.3 and earlier. RealVNC says cloud-hosted connectivity and manually configured direct connections (including offline licensed and on-premises deployments) are affected; TCP-only direct connections are not exposed.
items.summary: RealVNC advisory RVNC-2026-001 (CVE-2026-137738) fixes a memory-safety flaw in UDP-based connections that could let an attacker run code remotely, as root on certain platforms, or crash the software before authentication. It affects both RealVNC Viewer and Server apps on desktop and mobile. RealVNC rates it Critical, CVSS 9.8, and says it is not aware of exploitation in the wild. The CVE was not in the CISA KEV catalog at this check.
items.action: Update RealVNC Viewer and the Connect app to 8.6.2 or later, Server to 7.19.1 or later, Classic Viewer to 7.18.3 or later, and On-Demand Assist to 3.5.0 or later; check that mobile Viewer and Server apps have updated (Viewer 4.9.6, Server iOS 2.8.2, Server Android 2.8.4 or later).
steps: RealVNC Viewer, RealVNC Server and the RealVNC Connect app: download the latest version from https://www.realvnc.com/en/connect/download/ and install it on your devices.
RealVNC Classic Viewer: go to https://manage.realvnc.com, then Downloads, and download and install the latest version on your devices.
RealVNC On-Demand Assist: download the latest version from https://www.realvnc.help/en/ and advise end users to delete any older copies they downloaded.
Mobile apps should update automatically; to check, open RealVNC Viewer or RealVNC Server in Google Play or the App Store and tap Update.
items.gaps: FIRST EPSS returned no score for CVE-2026-137738. The CVE id comes from the NVD record, which links RealVNC's advisory; the advisory itself still lists the CVE as pending. RealVNC's release notes were not opened to confirm whether newer releases exist beyond the fixed versions.

items.priority_reason: CVE-2026-125274 lets any authenticated iControl SOAP user with at least the Guest role run system commands on BIG-IP, and fixed releases are named in F5's CVE record; exploitation was not established.
items.affected: Per F5's CVE record: BIG-IP iControl SOAP 21.0.0 before 21.1.0.3, 17.5.0 before 17.5.1.10, and 17.1.0 before 17.1.3.6; BIG-IQ 8.4.0 before 8.4.2.3. Versions past End of Technical Support are not evaluated. F5 says this is a control-plane issue with no data-plane exposure.
items.summary: F5's CVE-2026-125274 lets an authenticated iControl SOAP user with at least Guest privileges inject an unauthorized management request, which F5 says may allow running arbitrary system commands, creating or deleting files, or disabling services. It is a control-plane issue only. F5 scores it CVSS 3.1 8.8 and CVSS 4.0 8.7. Exploitation was not established, and it was not in the CISA KEV catalog at this check.
items.action: Update BIG-IP to 21.1.0.3, 17.5.1.10 or 17.1.3.6 or later on your branch, and BIG-IQ to 8.4.2.3 or later. Until then, remove iControl SOAP access for users who are not fully trusted and restrict iControl SOAP to trusted networks.
steps: Remove access to iControl SOAP for users who are not completely trusted; F5 says this is the only mitigation that applies while users still have access.

Block iControl SOAP access through self IP addresses: set Port Lockdown to Allow None for each self IP, or use Allow Custom and block the iControl SOAP port (TCP 443 by default, or your configured port). This can affect other services, including high availability.
Block iControl SOAP access through the management interface by restricting management access to trusted users and devices over a secure network.
items.gaps: F5 advisory K000163936 did not render, so fixed versions are taken from the affected ranges in F5's own CVE record and the newest BIG-IP release on each branch was not confirmed on F5's site.

items.priority_reason: CVE-2026-129448 lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run code on Apache Roller through the XML-RPC endpoint; Apache says it is being actively exploited and CISA added it to KEV on 2026-11-20.
items.affected: Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 per the CVE record; Apache says this is the same flaw an earlier CVE listed for 6.1.5, so every release before 6.1.6 should be treated as affected.
items.summary: Apache Roller has an unauthenticated deserialization flaw in its XML-RPC endpoint (CVE-2026-129448) that can let a remote attacker run arbitrary code. Apache rates it Critical, CVSS 9.8, and says it is being actively exploited. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on 2026-11-20. Turning off XML-RPC in the admin UI does not protect older versions.
items.action: Upgrade Apache Roller to 6.1.6 or later (6.1.7 is the current release). If you can't upgrade right away, apply Apache's interim mitigation below and restart Roller.
steps: Upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later from https://roller.apache.org/downloads/downloads.html.
If you cannot upgrade right away, set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, then restart Roller.
Do not rely on disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI; Apache says older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.
items.gaps: The Roller 6.1.7 release notes were not opened, so it is unconfirmed whether 6.1.7 adds further security fixes; the action names 6.1.6, the fixed release in Apache's advisory. FIRST EPSS score dated 2026-11-27. Ransomware use is listed as Unknown in KEV.

items.priority_reason: NoMachine confirms its Windows Personal Edition download was replaced for about 20 hours with a tampered installer that gives an attacker remote control of the computer.
items.affected: NoMachine says you may be affected if you downloaded nomachine-personal-edition_10.2.3_1_x64.exe from its website between 19 November 2026 13:43 UTC and 20 November 2026 10:00 UTC and ran it on a Windows computer. macOS, Linux, other NoMachine products and automatic updates were not affected.
items.summary: NoMachine says that during its security incident of 19 and 20 November 2026, the Personal Edition for Windows installer on its website was replaced by a tampered copy that adds a remote-access tool. That tool can run commands with administrator rights, read and change files, view the screen and reach other devices on the same network, and restarts itself every minute. NoMachine says the tampered file is unsigned, that the malware does not spread on its own, and that the safest fix is to reinstall Windows. A verified installer was restored on 20 November. There is no CVE.
items.action: If you downloaded and ran the NoMachine Personal Edition for Windows installer between 19 November 13:43 UTC and 20 November 10:00 UTC, treat that computer as fully exposed and follow NoMachine's steps, with reinstalling Windows as the safest fix.
steps: Check for a python folder inside the NoMachine folder (normally C:\Program Files\NoMachine\python), a running pythonw.exe in Task Manager, an installer with no embedded digital signature, or network connections to d137ukgg9ynlmn.cloudfront.net. Any one means the tampered installer was run.
If affected, disconnect the computer from the internet and do not type passwords on it.
From a different, clean device, change important passwords and turn on two-step verification.
Copy only personal files to a USB stick from the affected computer, then wipe it and reinstall Windows from clean media.
If you cannot reinstall right away, follow NoMachine's tested manual removal steps in its article while offline, then run a full antivirus scan.

Afterwards, change passwords again from a clean computer, including browser-saved passwords, saved NoMachine connection passwords and SSH keys kept on the affected computer, and reinstall NoMachine from the correct package.
If it was a work computer or held other people's data, tell your IT or security team.
items.gaps: NoMachine's related software-update notice SU11X00294 was not read separately. The vendor article does not name the attacker or say how the download was replaced.
